static_traits.name: Lin An
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends, but has not yet discussed feelings of self-blame and shame with them; somewhat tense relationships with friends, self-isolation tendencies
static_traits.medical_history: Never had similar psychological problems; never received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic; obvious self-criticism and negating tendencies; negative tone but willing to explore; skeptical of cognitive restructuring, Average cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: 'I keep feeling Self-denial and self-blame over bitcoin investment losses. I attribute this loss to my own ignorance and insufficient decision-making ability, and keep labeling myself 'I am an idiot'. I often treat financial losses as a direct reflection of my intelligence. These feelings often arise when I think about my financial situation or future investment opportunities; even though I try to rationalize and Learn more investment knowledge, the negative thoughts persist.'
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent self-blame and negative self-labeling have affected my decision-making ability and overall mental health, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: I am stupid / I am an idiot
Making mistakes means I am not smart / not capable enough

special_situations.event: Thinking about my financial situation or future investment opportunities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an investment loses money, it means I am stupid; the loss is a direct reflection of my intelligence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to prove their own competence through rationalization and self-education; at the same time avoids discussing with others to avoid embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is my fault; I am an idiot

special_situations.event: Recalls the situation where someone warned about Bitcoin risks and he still chose to invest
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must know and avoid such risks completely in advance, otherwise I am not smart enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Afterwards repeatedly blames oneself and compulsively demands oneself with 'should/must' standards

special_situations.event: Thinking again of investment losses when distracted at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative outcomes matter more than positive ones; must stay focused on mistakes at all times to prevent recurrence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly ruminating on loss details, ignoring existing efforts and positive factors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always mess things up; I bring it on myself

special_situations.event: Friends contact her or social opportunities arise; worried about mentioning investment losses
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not approve or I feel embarrassed, it means I do not deserve respect
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids socializing, choosing not to share inner feelings with friends to avoid evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Speaking out would be embarrassing; others may look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as capable and respectable
core_conflict.fear: Fears being judged as stupid or a failure, feeling shame at exposing vulnerability
defense_goal: Avoids external negative evaluation and shame through self-blame and self-isolation

object_relations.self_representation: A failure / stupid person (needs self-criticism to maintain a 'sense of control')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes cognitive restructuring or behavioral experiments, encouraging viewing losses from a more compassionate perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing reframing as 'self-deception/empty talk', finding it hard to allow a gentler view of oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a questioning and cautious tone, emphasizing logic and evidence, downplaying emotional experience, and avoiding in-depth exploration of shame

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether one confides in friends or seeks support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning potential anger/shame against the self, believing 'should not bother others', and intensifying self-criticism
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Refusing to proactively seek help, expressing in self-blaming language, restrained tone, maintaining self-isolation

manifestations: Tense relationships with friends, tending toward self-isolation
Avoiding talking about losses and feelings of shame
Bearing a heavy sense of self-responsibility for independently chosen investments
Attributes outcomes entirely to one's own ability and decisions

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to express outwardly or seek others to do something for them, turning the energy toward themselves instead (corresponding to 'impulse')
manifestations: Not seeking support from friends, turning emotional energy into self-blame and self-reproach
Choosing to process shame and guilt alone

contact_model.definition: Having unhealthy self-Reflection and excessive self-restriction and reproach, being overly cautious about contact (corresponding to 'autonomy')
manifestations: Repeatedly labels oneself negatively: 'I am an idiot'
Worrying 'it will be embarrassing', thus strictly restraining oneself and not expressing needs

contact_model.definition: Undigestedly treating external rules and expectations as one's own standards or absolute truth (corresponding to 'rejection')
manifestations: Demands self with rigid standards such as 'I should have known earlier'
Internalizes others' reminders about risk into harsh self-norms

positive_force: Has rational analysis and Learning ability (Engineer background, previously actively Learned investment knowledge)
Has several close friends as potential support resources
Able to self-Reflect, identify and describe distress and impact (Work and sleep changes, etc.)
Willing to seek professional help to improve the situation
negative_force: Negative self-labeling and excessive self-blame (personalizing losses as an intelligence problem)
Social Withdrawal and avoiding help-seeking lead to Decreased support
Persistent rumination on losses and ignoring positive factors (mental filtering)
Sleep disturbance and fatigue weaken cognitive resources and emotional regulation

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-blame and negative self-labeling (such as 'I am an idiot')
antecedent: Thinking about financial situation or future investment opportunities
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizing financial losses as a direct reflection of intelligence and ability, forming a stable negative core belief
target_behavior.function: Maintains a 'sense of control' over risks and consequences through self-criticism, while avoiding external evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased decision-making ability, impaired overall mental health, worsened Low mood and shame

antecedent: Friends reaching out or social opportunities arising
Possibly bringing up topics of losses and embarrassment
target_behavior.core_reason: Fear of shame and being judged, tending to blame problems on oneself and avoid exposing vulnerability
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with friends, Weakened support system, increased Loneliness

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep disturbance(Difficulty falling asleep,Declining sleep quality)
antecedent: Repeatedly recalling investment losses and mistakes before sleep
Thinking about possible risks of future investment at night
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative automatic thoughts driven by rumination and worry remain activated, trying to gain certainty and control through thinking
target_behavior.function: Using overthinking to prevent future errors (surface control), actually increasing arousal and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Daytime fatigue, Decreased attention, mood easily fluctuating

target_behavior.behavior: Unfocused Work attention and declining performance
antecedent: Interrupted at work by negative automatic thoughts about losses
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative self-evaluation occupies cognitive resources, reinforcing the failure–self-blame cycle
target_behavior.function: Psychologically avoids facing task load and feelings of failure
target_behavior.consequence: Declining performance in the Engineer role, further worsening Self-denial
